newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank of India sees 97/98 profit at 6.5 bln rupees.
newsitem.headline: Bank of India sees 97/98 profit at 6.5 bln rupees.

text.p: State-run Bank of India on Wednesday said it boosted its post-tax profit to a provisional 4.48 billion rupees ($125 million) for the year ended March 31, 1997 (April-March), up from 2.76 billion rupees a year ago.

The bank, whose shares are to be listed on India's leading stock exchanges over the next few days, is projecting a "conservative" post-tax profit of 6.5 billion rupees for 1997/98, its outgoing chairman Gordhan Kathuria told reporters.
"My friends in the Bombay Stock Exchange say it (the bank's stock) should be listed at 70-75 rupees," Kathuria said.
The bank will consider an overseas equity issue later in the year, oncen the share touches the 100 rupee mark, he said.
The bank's maiden public issue of shares of 10 rupees face value at 45 rupees a share to raise 6.75 billion rupees was oversubscribed in February this year.
The issue boosted the bank's capital adequacy to 11 percent.
Kathuria said the bank's overseas operations were doing very well and new branches would be established in five countries.
"Out of 4.48 billion (provisional profit for 1996/97), 1.25 billion came from overeas operations," Kathuria said.
Branches are proposed to be set up in the near future in Indonesia, Malaysia, Ghana, Trinidad and Australia.
The bank disbursed 40 percent out of $400 million worth of loan applications under India's external commercial borrowing (ECB) from January to April this year, he said.
The bulk of these loans are for $3.0 million for which no prior Reserve Bank of India approval is necessary, he said.
"We have some 60.0 billion rupees forex deposit base which we are parking in our foreign offices," he said.
Bank of India has also joined loan syndications to Indian firms along with Japanese banks such as Sumitomo Bank and Asahi Bank, Kathuria said.
Bank of India's net non-performing assets have been reduced to 5.0 percent during 1996/97 from 7.0 percent a year ago.
"It is the lowest among comparable banks and in line with international norms," he said. ($1.00=35.75)
